title: The digestive system

draft.title: The digestive system
card: the physical breaking of food into smaller pieces, such as chewing and the churning of the stomach. It does not change the food's chemicals.
enzymes break large molecules into small ones. For example, amylase in saliva starts to break starch into sugars.
Food passes through the mouth, oesophagus, stomach and small intestine. The liver and pancreas help digestion, but food does not pass through them.
Absorption happens mostly in the small intestine. Its folds and villi give a large surface area, so digested nutrients pass into the blood.
draft.remember: Food is broken down physically and chemically, then absorbed in the small intestine.

a.q: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed into the blood?
opts: The small intestine
The stomach
The oesophagus
The mouth
a.why: The small intestine has folds and villi that give a large surface area for absorption. The stomach mainly churns food and starts chemical digestion, so it is not the main site of absorption.
a.clue: Think about where villi are found.

b.q: Jin chews a piece of bread for a long time and notices it starts to taste sweet. What best explains this?
opts: Amylase in saliva is breaking starch into sugars
Chewing is turning starch into sugars mechanically
The stomach is absorbing sugars from the bread
Villi in the mouth are absorbing the starch
b.why: Amylase is an enzyme, so it causes chemical digestion of starch into sugars. Chewing is mechanical digestion, which makes smaller pieces but does not change the starch into sugar.
b.clue: Which type of digestion changes the chemicals in food?

b.best: Amylase in saliva is breaking starch into sugars

problems.detail: Why (a) says the stomach 'starts chemical digestion', but the card says chemical digestion starts in the mouth with salivary amylase. The stomach starts protein digestion, not chemical digestion overall, so the why contradicts the card.

The list 'Food passes through the mouth, oesophagus, stomach and small intestine' reads as the complete path and leaves out the large intestine. Students may think the tract ends at the small intestine. Adding 'then the large intestine' or 'includes' would fix this.
